bib.title: The Probabilistic Relevance Framework: BM25 and Beyond

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "The Probabilistic Relevance Framework: BM25 and Beyond", Stephen Robertson and Hugo Zaragoza, Foundations and Trends in Information Retrieval Vol. 3, No. 4 (2009) 333–389, DOI 10.1561/1500000019.

COVERAGE: I read all 99,228 of 99,228 characters (59 PDF pages), from the table of contents through the conclusions. I skimmed the references for origins. I did not run the figure-caption script. Figure captions come from the extracted text.

CLAIMS
- claim: The classic BM25 weight divides tf by a soft length normaliser B, applies the saturation tf'/(k1+tf'), and multiplies by the RSJ weight. A document's score is the sum of these weights over the query terms.
  number: Eq. 3.12 to 3.15
  setup: General derivation, with no particular corpus.
  quote: "B := ( (1 − b)+ b dlavdl ), 0 ≤ b ≤ 1 (3.12)" … "wBM25i (tf )= tf ′k1 + tf ′ wRSJi (3.14) = tfk1 ((1 − b)+ b dlavdl ) + tf wRSJi (3.15) This is the classic BM25 term-weighting and document-scoring function." (The fractions are flattened in extraction.)
  where: p. 359–360, about chars 45,000–46,700
- claim: The (k1+1) factor in the numerator, which the note's formula includes, is a variant. It does not change the ranking. It only makes one occurrence score the same as the RSJ weight alone.
  number: none
  setup: Section 3.5.1, variations on BM25.
  quote: "A common variant is to add a ( k1 + 1) component to the numerator of the saturation function. This is the same for all terms, and therefore does not aﬀect the ranking produced."
  where: p. 361
- claim: k1 comes from fitting a simple curve to the saturating term-weight shape that Harter's 2-Poisson eliteness model produces. The weight rises with tf toward an asymptote, the binary eliteness (BIM) weight. That limit is what "saturation" means.
  number: tf/(k+tf), Eq. 3.10
  setup: The 2-Poisson model assumes fixed-length documents.
  quote: "the authors of BM25 decided to ﬁt a simple parametric curve to this shape. The following one-parameter function was chosen: tf k + tf for some k> 0 (3.10)"; "any one term's contribution to the document score cannot exceed a saturation point (the asymptotic limit)"
  where: p. 355–357
- claim: b comes from soft length normalisation between two hypotheses. "Verbosity" would mean normalising tf fully by length. "Scope" would mean not normalising at all. b=1 gives full normalisation and b=0 switches it off.
  number: b between 0 and 1
  setup: Section 3.4.5.
  quote: "Thus setting b = 1 will perform full document-length normalisation, while b = 0 will switch normalisation oﬀ."
  where: p. 359
- claim: The model gives no guidance on k1 and b, and the authors call this a limitation. Experiments find a range of values that works reasonably well, but the best values depend on the documents and queries.
  number: 0.5<b<0.8, 1.2<k1<2
  setup: Many retrieval experiments, not fully referenced.
  quote: "the model provides no guid- ance on how these should be set. This may be regarded as a limi- tation of the model." … "values s u c ha s0.5 <b< 0.8 and 1 .2 <k 1 < 2 are reasonably good in many circumstances. However, there is also evidence that optimal values do depend on other factors (such as the type of documents or queries)."
  where: p. 360–361
- claim: Some published versions fix b=0.5 and k1=2. Experiments favour a lower k1 and a higher b. (The note's default of b=0.75 sits inside the 0.5–0.8 range above. The source never states 0.75 itself.)
  number: b=0.5, k1=2
  setup: Published BM25 variants.
  quote: "A common combination would be b =0 .5 and k1 = 2. (However, many experiments suggest a somewhat lower value of k1 and a somewhat higher value of b.)"
  where: p. 361
- claim: Without relevance information, the RSJ weight with R=r=0 reduces to an IDF form with 0.5 smoothing. That is the same as setting P(t|rel)=0.5.
  number: Eq. 3.3
  setup: No relevance judgements; the complement method treats the whole collection as non-relevant.
  quote: "All this can be achieved by setting R = ri = 0 in the RSJ formula (3.2) — this is equivalent to settingP(ti |rel) = 0.5" … "wIDFi = logN − ni +0 .5ni +0 .5 (3.3)" (that is, log((N−n+0.5)/(n+0.5)))
  where: p. 349
- claim: The 0.5 pseudo-count exists because raw ratios inside a log can give infinite weights. The source does NOT discuss the negative IDF this form gives for terms in more than half the documents. See LIMITS.
  number: 0.5
  setup: RSJ estimation.
  quote: "the combination of a ratio of proba- bilities and a log function may yield (positive or negative) inﬁnities as estimates … introduces a small pseudo-count of frequency 0.5."
  where: p. 348
- claim: BM25F weights fields (streams) before saturation. It sums the stream-weighted, per-stream length-normalised tf for each term, then applies saturation once. The reasoning is that eliteness belongs to the term and document, so it is shared across fields. Scoring each field with BM25 and adding the scores is the wrong order.
  number: Eq. 3.19–3.21
  setup: There is one flat set of fields shared by all documents, for example title, body and anchor.
  quote: "we should combine evidence across terms and streams in the opposite order to that suggested above: ﬁrst streams, then terms." "~tf i = S∑ s=1 vs tf si Bs (3.19)" "wBM25Fi = ~tf i k1 + ~tf i wRSJi (3.21)"
  where: p. 362–364
- claim: Tuned BM25F parameters from TREC 2003 web tasks are far from plain-BM25 defaults, because field weights rescale tf.
  number: k1 27.5 (TD), 4.9 (NP); v_title 38.4 / 13.5
  setup: Table 3.1, from [62]; topic distillation (TD) and named page (NP) tasks, TREC 2003.
  quote: "k1 27.5 4.9 btitle 0.95 0.6 bbody 0.7 0.5 banchor 0.6 0.6 vtitle 38.4 13.5 vbody 1.0 1.0 vanchor 35 11.5"
  where: p. 365
- claim: With integer weights, simple BM25F is the same as ordinary BM25 run on a document whose fields have been copied that many times.
  number: v_title=5
  setup: Simple version (Eq. 3.18) only.
  quote: "formula 3.18 is equivalent to 3.15 applied to a document in which the title has been replicated ﬁve times and the abstract twice."
  where: p. 365
- claim: Computing IDF over the whole collection and ignoring fields worked in practice, but it can break down.
  number: none
  setup: BM25F.
  quote: "it can lead to degener- ate cases (e.g., when a stream is extremely verbose and contains most terms for most documents). The proper deﬁnition of IDF in this con- text requires further research"
  where: p. 364
- claim: A linear tf, as in tf·idf, only follows from the model in the special case where eliteness equals relevance. Otherwise, saturating tf has repeatedly beaten traditional tf·idf.
  number: none
  setup: Section 3.4.3.
  quote: "the non-linear, saturating function of tf developed below (also combined with anidf component) has frequently been shown to work better than traditional tf *idf ."
  where: p. 356
- claim: Query-independent features are added as extra terms with their own transforms. This explains why BM25F + log(PageRank) works.
  number: none
  setup: Section 3.7.
  quote: "This development can explain for example why simple scoring functions such as BM25F(q,d)+log(PageRank (d)) may work well in practice"
  where: p. 367
- claim: When fields are added, k1 should be rescaled by how much the field weights change the average length.
  number: Eq. 5.1
  setup: BM25F tuning.
  quote: "kBM25F1 ≈ kBM251 ∑ s vsavsl s∑ s avsl s (5.1)"
  where: p. 382
- claim: BM25 and BM25F are robust to their parameters, but tuning still gives significant gains on a new collection.
  number: none
  setup: Section 5.
  quote: "small changes in the parameter values (or in the collection) do not produce large changes in accuracy or relevance. Nevertheless signiﬁcant gains in relevance can be obtained by properly optimising the parameters"
  where: p. 377

LIMITS:
- What the framework does not handle:
  - Positions and proximity. "For the most part the PRF ignores positional information". The gains from position-aware variants "are small".
  - Calibrated probabilities. The rank-preserving steps throw away what an explicit P(rel) would need, so the model must be "considerably modiﬁed" for uses such as filtering.
  - Graded relevance, or relevance that depends on other documents. Both assumptions are "arguable".
  - Term independence, which is "clearly a much more arguable step".
  - Parameter guidance. k1 and b come from experiments, not from the model.
  - Field-aware IDF, which is still open.
  - Synonymy. Query expansion "may worsen the term independence assumption".
- Blind feedback "tends to fail on some queries, particularly on queries that are diﬃcult to start with".
- The source is "not primarily an experimental survey". Most "works well" claims are not referenced to experiments.
- Negative IDF is not discussed. The IDF form log((N−n+0.5)/(n+0.5)) goes negative when n > N/2, but the text never says so. BM25+ is not mentioned either. Cite those claims to another source.
- Dated material: the 2009 open-source list says Lucene "does not implement BM25" and only MG4J fully implements BM25F. Lucene has used BM25 by default for a long time since then. The gradient learning-to-rank discussion predates neural retrieval.

BUILDS ON:
- Harter 1975 (2-Poisson eliteness)
- Robertson & Sparck Jones 1977 (RSJ weight)
- Robertson 1977 (PRP)
- Robertson, van Rijsbergen & Porter 1981
- Robertson & Walker 1994, SIGIR (original BM25)
- Cooper 1995 (linked dependence)
- Maron & Kuhns 1960
- Sparck Jones, Walker & Robertson 2000 (Parts 1–2)
- Robertson, Zaragoza & Taylor 2004 CIKM (simple BM25F)
- Zaragoza et al. TREC 2004 (BM25F with per-field b)
- Craswell et al. 2005 (non-textual features)

CODE: None. The source has formulas only. Note that PF/Tijah uses a different IDF: "PF/Tijah uses idf= logN +0.5n+0.5" (p. 370, footnote).

FIGURES:
- Fig. 3.3, p. 358: "Saturation functions generated by Equation (3.10) with raw frequencies (left) and with frequencies normalised using Equation (3.13) ( right). Stronger saturation is obtained with lower values of k (left) and with shorter documents ( right). For the plot on the right we used k = 1 and b =0 .5." This shows the effect of k1 and of length together, faster than a sweep table does.
- Fig. 3.2, p. 357: "Left: some possible saturation functions. Right: saturation functions generated by the 2-Poisson model." This explains why tf/(k+tf) was chosen.
- Fig. 3.1, p. 353: graphical model of eliteness.
- Figs. 5.1 and 5.2, p. 380: examples of robust line search and promising-directions search.

PROBLEMS:
- Extraction flattened the fractions and dropped the overbars. For example, "P(d|rel,q)P(d|rel,q)" has lost the bar marking the non-relevant term, so read the quotes with that in mind.
- Some spaces were inserted ("s u c ha s0.5", "k 1").
- "Sprck Jones" has lost its diacritic.
- pypdf warned that fontTools was missing, but the text was otherwise readable.
- There were no embedded instructions.

Note for the caller: the note's slide line about "1.3×" and its saturation table are consistent with this source's tf/(k1+tf) form. The source does not state b=0.75 as a default.
